title: Problem Overview
content:
**Erdős Problem #619: Decreasing Diameter of Triangle-Free Graphs**

**Question (OPEN):** Does there exist c > 0 such that h₄(G) < (1-c)n for all connected triangle-free graphs G on n vertices?

**Known bounds:**
- h₃(G) ≤ n
- h₄(G) ≤ ? (OPEN)
- h₅(G) ≤ (n-1)/2

**Key constraint:** Graph must remain triangle-free after adding edges.
mathContext: h_r(G) = min edges to add to achieve diameter r while staying triangle-free. Introduced by Erdős-Gyárfás-Ruszinkó (1998).

title: Triangle-Free, Diameter, and Core Definitions
content:
**TriangleFree(G):** A graph with no K₃ subgraphs — for all vertices a, b, c, it is impossible that a-b, b-c, and c-a are all edges.

**diameter(G):** The supremum of pairwise distances in G.

**HasDiameter / HasDiameterAtMost:** Predicates for exact and bounded diameter.

Examples of triangle-free graphs: paths, even cycles, bipartite graphs, Petersen graph.
mathContext: $G$ is triangle-free if $\forall a, b, c \in V(G)$: $\neg(ab \in E \wedge bc \in E \wedge ca \in E)$. The diameter $\text{diam}(G) = \max_{u,v} d(u,v)$ measures the worst-case distance.

title: Edge Addition and h_r(G)
content:
**addEdges(G, E):** Constructs a new graph by adding edges E to G. The definition proves symmetry and looplessness, making it a valid SimpleGraph.

**h(G, r):** The central function — the minimum number of edges to add to G to achieve diameter ≤ r while preserving the triangle-free property. Defined via sInf over all valid edge sets.

**h_exact(G, r):** Variant requiring diameter exactly r.

title: Known Results (Erdős-Gyárfás-Ruszinkó 1998)
content:
**h₃(G) ≤ n:** For any connected triangle-free graph G on n vertices, at most n edges suffice to reduce diameter to 3.

**h₃(G) ≥ n - c:** This bound is tight — there exist graphs needing nearly n edges for diameter 3.

**h₅(G) ≤ (n-1)/2:** Much fewer edges suffice for diameter 5.

The dramatic drop from h₃ ~ n to h₅ ~ n/2 is what makes the intermediate h₄ case so intriguing.
mathContext: These results are from Erdős, Gyárfás, and Ruszinkó's 1998 paper that introduced the h_r function.

title: The Erdős Question (OPEN)
content:
**erdos_619_question:** Does there exist c > 0 such that h₄(G) < (1-c)n for all connected triangle-free G on n vertices?

In other words: can we always save a constant fraction of n edges when targeting diameter 4? Neither a proof nor counterexample is known.

**erdos_619_upper_bound_form:** Equivalent formulation as h₄(G) < n - εn.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of the erdős question (open)

title: Without Triangle-Free Constraint (AGR 2000)
content:
**without_triangle_free_constraint:** When triangles are allowed, n/2 edges always suffice for diameter 4 (Alon-Gyárfás-Ruszinkó 2000).

This shows the triangle-free constraint fundamentally changes the problem. The most natural shortcut edges often create triangles, so forbidding them makes diameter reduction much harder.
mathContext: Comparison with the unconstrained case reveals the essential difficulty of the triangle-free requirement.

title: Path Graph Example
content:
**pathGraph(n):** The path on n vertices (v₀-v₁-...-v_{n-1}), defined as a SimpleGraph on Fin n with adjacency i↔j iff |i-j|=1. The definition includes proofs of symmetry and looplessness.

**path_is_triangle_free:** Paths contain no triangles (axiomatized).
**path_diameter:** The path Pₙ has diameter n-1 (axiomatized).

Paths are natural test cases for h_r: they have maximum possible diameter, requiring many edges to reduce it.

title: h_r Monotonicity
content:
**h_monotone:** h(G, r) ≥ h(G, r+1) — achieving smaller diameter requires at least as many edges as achieving larger diameter.

This gives the chain: h₃(G) ≥ h₄(G) ≥ h₅(G).

Combined with the known bounds h₃ ≤ n and h₅ ≤ (n-1)/2, monotonicity constrains h₄ to lie between (n-1)/2 and n.
mathContext: See annotation content for formal details of h_r monotonicity

title: Summary and Partial Results
content:
**erdos_619:** The main open question, defined as erdos_619_question.

**erdos_619_partial_results:** For any connected triangle-free G on n vertices:
- h(G, 3) ≤ n
- h(G, 5) ≤ (n-1)/2

Proved by combining h3_upper_bound and h5_upper_bound axioms. These are the established bounds from Erdős-Gyárfás-Ruszinkó (1998), with the h₄ gap remaining open.
